lots.guide_summary: Surviving close SOLD results at Gowans, Hobart (hammer, premium extra, all AUD): sets of six Edwardian or oak chairs $30, $50 and $110; set of four $80; set of eight $180; a pair of the same golden oak T-back type $25. Guide for a set of six is $30 to $110 hammer, all of it SOLD evidence. One category-guide dealer ASKING price of $1,500 (restored, different style) is shown for context only and not used in the range. No UNSOLD entries. No currency conversion needed.
lots.working: No exact same-style SOLD result exists; the closest sets of six of the same era in similar tidy order are the Gowans $50 (370697) and $110 (394688) sets, with a plainer turned-leg set at $30 (409445) treated as a lower-quality type. keep_max: $50 / 1.22 = $40.98, rounded down to $40 hammer (all-in $48.80). If you treat the $30 set as same-item, keep_max falls to $30 / 1.22 = $24.59, so $20. flip_max: likely resale about $50 hammer at a Tasmanian room (from $50 and $30 to $110 results), less about 15% seller commission and fees ($7.50), no outbound postage (local pickup), leaves $42.50; / 2.44 = $17.42, rounded down to $15. Not a flip proposition. Buyer premium 22% incl GST; inbound freight $0 (local pickup at 9 Goodman Crt, Invermay).
lots.confidence_reason: Identification clear from four photos and there is no mark to read, but there is no exact same-style SOLD result: several close Tasmanian SOLD results were checked in the API with photos viewed, all of differing style. Timber not confirmed.

WebSearch budget was exhausted, so no Armitage past results could be searched.
lots.key_photo_findings: Six matching chairs, all present. Carved roundel with stylised Art Nouveau double scroll on a punched ground, three pierced slats, shaped top rail, cabriole front legs, stretchers. Close fine grain with no clear medullary ray fleck, so 'English oak' unconfirmed; form is closer to American golden oak chairs of c.1900-1915. No label or stamp; undersides not shown.
lots.condition: Good: clean even finish with light wear, seat fabric tidy with a few small marks, no visible breaks or repairs. Joints and seat frames not shown.
lots.question_for_armitage: Are all six chairs firm with no loose joints or repairs, and is there any maker's label or stamp under the seats? What makes you call the timber English oak?
